newsitem.title: DENMARK: Copenhagen bourse keeps bond floor at four pct.
newsitem.headline: Copenhagen bourse keeps bond floor at four pct.

text.p: The Copenhagen Stock Exchange said on Thursday that it would retain the current four percent rate floor for debt instruments until its next scheduled review, in June 1997, if market conditions allowed.
"If the market rate should change considerably during this period the Copenhagen Stock Exchange may announce a new minimum rate," a bourse statement said.

An unscheduled October 22 adjustment in the floor to four percent from six percent triggered a flood of four percent bonds, attractive to local private investors for whom the low coupon provides tax advantages under Danish law.

Issuance of four percent bonds since the reduction is well over 20 billion crowns but analysts expect the flow of funds to corporate paper to diminish when the government issues its own four percent treasury note on January 7.
The floor rate is usually fixed twice-yearly -- in June and December -- according to an average of yields on specified fixed-interest, government and mortgage-backed bonds

It was left unchanged at six percent last June but cut in an extraordinary October adjustment after several expiring mortgage-backed bonds were replaced by smaller series, reducing the average. --Copenhagen newsroom +45 33 969650
